text: We are a manufacturer in Hobart looking to automate order processing, shop-floor data capture, and operations without replacing our ERP. Which automation and Power Platform consultants should we speak to?

result.keyword: We are a manufacturer in Hobart looking to automate order processing, shop-floor data capture, and operations without replacing our ERP. Which automation and Power Platform consultants should we speak to?
result.markdown:
For a Hobart manufacturer that wants to automate order processing, capture shop-floor data and streamline operations **without replacing its existing ERP**, I would shortlist two types of consultants: Microsoft Power Platform specialists for business workflows and applications, and industrial automation specialists for production-floor systems.

The key is to find a partner who can integrate with your current ERP, rather than use automation as a reason to sell you a new one.

## My recommended shortlist

![Power Apps Automation for Ceramic Manufacturing | Softree Technology Case Studies](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/xXJ1Em7sPFHHh8ANxwsAiSqWqIuRl-GwcwX9IgTBV0OAwJd0V-sfyligUrHWRUIqr5K9hpTu75aVpvFzBkj_EglEBjM8soU5IvUuaeL9qaVjH0-TEM3DCTvcovLylUCIk35jHVyGsxg4LVHFUtS4EgNprm0Abglih9UDY0ieLTrBUd9fi3bzIlkjw4sDLp-F?purpose=fullsize)

## 1\. Inturing

(Best fit for your brief)

Australian-wide delivery · Power Platform specialist

Inturing explicitly targets manufacturers running existing ERP, CRM and manufacturing systems. Its services include automated order processing, Power Apps for shop-floor capture, Power Automate workflows, system integration and operational dashboards—all without an ERP replacement. **Ask them about\:** email/PDF order extraction, order validation against your ERP, production and quality data capture, and exception handling.

[Website: inturing.com.au](https://inturing.com.au/)

## 2\. Cyberhaven Technologies

Hobart-based · Workflow automation and RPA

A local option offering Microsoft Power Automate, robotic process automation (RPA), API integration and document processing. Its stated capabilities include manufacturing, logistics and order-processing workflows. [cyberhaven.com.au](https://cyberhaven.com.au/our-services/system-automation-services-in-hobart/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Ask them about\:** automating repetitive ERP data entry, handling customer orders received in different formats, and integrating existing applications.

Contact: [cyberhaven.com.au](https://cyberhaven.com.au/our-services/system-automation-services-in-hobart/)

Confirm their experience building Power Apps and supporting manufacturing deployments, rather than only office-based RPA.

## 5\. Buftec

Hobart-based · ERP integration, databases and legacy systems

Buftec works across business applications, databases, APIs, reporting and legacy-system modernisation, with an emphasis on protecting live production systems. [www.buftec.com](https://www.buftec.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Ask them about\:** assessing your ERP's integration options, database access, APIs and safe ways to automate data exchange.

Contact: [buftec.com](https://www.buftec.com/)

Treat this as a technical integration candidate, not a confirmed specialist Power Platform partner.

## Where the local consultants are


Also worth considering is UXC Eclipse, now associated with DXC, which has a Hobart presence and Microsoft business applications experience. It may be worth contacting for larger-scale Microsoft integration requirements, particularly if your ERP is already Microsoft Dynamics. Confirm the proposed team's current Power Platform delivery experience before engaging.

## How I would divide the work

For your three objectives, I would initially approach **Inturing, Cyberhaven and SAGE Automation**\. Together, those conversations should help establish whether you need a single Power Platform delivery partner or a business-automation and industrial-automation pairing.

**Order processing**

Use Power Automate to ingest orders from email or documents, validate required fields, route exceptions for approval, and create or update ERP records through supported interfaces.

**Shop-floor data capture**

Use Power Apps for operator inputs, inspections, scrap and downtime records. If data needs to come directly from machinery, involve an industrial automation specialist to connect the control systems safely.

**Operations visibility**

Use Power BI for production, order backlog, delivery performance and quality dashboards, with the ERP remaining the authoritative source for transactional data.

## Questions to ask before selecting a partner

1. **Have you integrated Power Platform with our particular ERP?** Ask for a relevant reference, not just a list of connectors.
2. Can you use our ERP's APIs or supported integration interfaces instead of relying on fragile screen-clicking automation?
3. How will you prevent duplicate orders, handle failed integrations and reconcile data?
4. Can shop-floor apps work on shared tablets or industrial devices, including areas with unreliable connectivity?
5. Will we own the solution, documentation, flows, apps and support arrangements after handover?
6. Can you deliver a fixed-scope pilot with measurable outcomes before committing to a broader programme?

My preference would be to start with a small order-processing pilot, prove that it integrates reliably with your existing ERP, and then extend the architecture to shop-floor capture.

## One question that would sharpen the shortlist

**Which ERP are you currently running?** For example, Pronto Xi, MYOB Advanced, SAP, Epicor, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, or a custom/legacy system.

The ERP name will help distinguish consultants with relevant integration experience from those who offer general Power Platform development but may struggle with your specific manufacturing environment.
